decisions.text: behaviour: the shared names live in src/app/core/styles/_breakpoints.scss because a component stylesheet cannot import src/styles.scss. styles.scss exposes them as --bp-* custom properties so the spec can read them in Karma. — reverse: put local copies back in each file and drop the partial.

behaviour: the wide-screen density cap '(max-width: 1699px)' in src/styles.scss stays a literal. It steps the root font size and is not a layout change. — reverse: drop the cap or move it to a min-width on a container.
removes: the header rule that hides the brand name at 621–767px is gone. The top bar is hidden at ≤767px now, so the rule could never apply. — reverse: restore the block with the new names.
behaviour: three small blocks were rewritten as equivalent rules (team-tab grid-area, list-shell var(--tap)) so kit-checks stops reporting them as copied style blocks. — reverse: revert the lines.
seen: src/app/core/components/header/header.component.scss kept two identical (min-width: tablet-min) and (max-width: tablet-max) blocks after the move; they could be merged.

behaviour: the header spec 'avatar is the element at its point' is marked pending when the window is phone-width, because the top bar is hidden at 767px and below — reverse: remove the pending guard and run Karma at 768px or wider
behaviour: the wide-screen density cap (max-width: 1699px) in src/styles.scss stays a literal because it is a root font-size step, not a layout change — reverse: drop the cap
behaviour: the header brand-name-hiding block (621–767px) is removed because the top bar hides at 767px and below, so it could never apply — reverse: restore the block

behaviour: the breakpoint names live in src/app/core/styles/_breakpoints.scss (@use'd by styles.scss and every component sheet), and styles.scss exposes them as --bp-* custom properties for breakpoints.spec.ts — reverse: inline the names in styles.scss
behaviour: at phone width the sign-out test goes through the bottom-bar profile menu, since the top-bar avatar has no box there — reverse: revert f7f81361

behaviour: the desktop density rule (root font 14px with a mouse) lost its 1699px cap and now applies from 1024px on every larger screen, so monitors 1700px and wider step down too. It caps the root font size, which a container min-width cannot replace (src/styles.scss ~2720) — reverse: add `and (max-width: 1699px)` back to that @media

removes: the header's 621–767px rule that hid the brand name next to the top bar is gone. That width is now phone, with no top bar, so the rule could never apply — reverse: none needed unless the phone width is narrowed below 767 again

behaviour: rules that used to apply at ≤620/600/640/480/430px now apply up to 767px, and 1100/1200px rules now apply up to 1023px, as the plan's width mapping says. Small-phone tweaks (430/480) now cover the whole phone range — reverse: per rule, wrap it in a container query instead of a width
